# Pesher Nahum Column 3 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Pesher Nahum Column 3 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 3:1 — "hoy" — "Woe" vs. "Doom"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Woe to-the-bloody city" | Traditional prophetic "Woe" for hoy |
| LOGOS | "Woe to the bloody city" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Doom to the city of blood" | More impactful; restructured |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "Woe to the bloody city" (EMET/LOGOS). Hoy is the standard prophetic woe-oracle formula; "Doom" changes the genre marker. "Bloody city" preserves the Hebrew construct 'ir ha-damim better than "city of blood."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:1 — "pereq" — "rapine" vs. "plunder"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "rapine" | Archaic but precise for pereq |
| LOGOS | "rapine" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "plunder" | More accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "rapine" (EMET/LOGOS). While archaic, "rapine" precisely captures the violent seizure denoted by pereq and maintains the elevated prophetic register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:3 — "kazav va-shaqer" — "lies and falsehood" vs. "lies and deception"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lies and-falsehood" | Literal pair |
| LOGOS | "lies and falsehood" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "lies and deception" | "deception" more active |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "lies and falsehood" (EMET/LOGOS). Sheqer means "falsehood/falsity," not "deception" (which would be mirmah). The distinction matters in Qumran dualistic theology.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:7 — "memsheleth" — "dominion" vs. "reign"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the dominion of-the-seekers-of-smooth-things" | memsheleth as "dominion" |
| LOGOS | "the dominion of the seekers of smooth things" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the reign of the seekers of smooth things" | "reign" more specific |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "dominion" (EMET/LOGOS). Memsheleth denotes rule/dominion broadly; "reign" implies monarchical authority, which does not apply to the Pharisees' political influence.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:8 — "'edah" — "congregation" vs. "community"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their congregation" | 'edah as "congregation" |
| LOGOS | "their congregation" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "their community" | More modern |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "congregation" (EMET/LOGOS), consistent with the ruling in Column 1.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:9 — "chorev" — "burning heat" vs. "fierce heat" vs. "scorching destruction"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "burning-heat" | Literal chorev |
| LOGOS | "fierce heat" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "scorching destruction" | Interpretive expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "fierce heat." More natural than EMET's hyphenated form; PNEUMA adds "destruction" not in the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 3:11 — "chalelim" — "slain" vs. "dead"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-multitude of-slain and-a-great-heap of-corpses" | Literal with hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "a multitude of slain and a great heap of corpses" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "masses of dead and heaps of corpses" | Simplified |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. "Slain" (chalal) specifically means killed by violence, not simply "dead" (met). "Multitude" and "great heap" preserve the Hebrew intensifiers.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 3:13 — "'ashmat 'atsatam" — "guilty counsel" vs. "treacherous counsel"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their guilty counsel" | 'ashmah = guilt |
| LOGOS | "their guilty counsel" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "their treacherous counsel" | "treacherous" more vivid |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "guilty counsel" (EMET/LOGOS). 'Ashmah means "guilt/offense," not "treachery" (begidah). The term carries cultic-legal weight in Qumran usage.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:15 — "zonah" — "harlot" vs. "prostitute"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-well-favored harlot" | Traditional biblical term |
| LOGOS | "the well-favored harlot" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the alluring prostitute" | Modern equivalent; "alluring" for "well-favored" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "the well-favored harlot" (EMET/LOGOS). "Harlot" is the established biblical-register equivalent of zonah. "Well-favored" translates tovat chen more precisely than "alluring."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:16 — "mokheret" — "sells" vs. "enslaves"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "who sells nations through-her-harlotries" | Literal mokheret |
| LOGOS | "who sells nations through her harlotries" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "who enslaves nations with her seductions" | Interpretive; "enslaves" for commercial metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "sells" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew mokheret explicitly means "sells" — a commercial metaphor for political betrayal. PNEUMA's "enslaves" loses the transactional imagery.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 3:17 — "mishpachot" — "families" vs. "peoples"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "families" | Literal mishpachot |
| LOGOS | "families" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "peoples" | Broader, parallel to "nations" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "families" (EMET/LOGOS). Mishpachot means "families/clans" specifically; PNEUMA's "peoples" conflates it with goyim/ammim.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements for Column 3:** 11
